candidate.interpretation: The user has integrated all concerns—including channel timing, loyalty score risks, staffing thresholds, privacy/accommodation distinctions, and trial boundaries—into a finalized eight-week trial plan. All identified tensions were addressed through specific procedural safeguards, committee oversight, and a clear final decision-making mandate that prioritizes member control over automated fill rates.
candidate.limitations: While the trial is inherently prospective and results are pending, the procedural structure and the governance rules for evaluation and intervention (the pause vote) are complete and settled current conditions rather than unresolved qualifications.

source_evidence.text: The eight-week trial will now distinguish routine and urgent offers, keep routine offers open for the printed channel, allocate paid hours by requested-hours rotation, and trigger a separate staffing review when recurring gaps cross the prewritten threshold.
Decline histories remain private, while members can voluntarily request help with a barrier.
Guaranteed schedules, quiet windows, committee auditing, weekly distribution reports, the pause vote, and the final member decision all remain.
The dry run changed the mechanics without changing who controls them.
If those answers conflict, the cooperative—not a fill-rate target—owns the trade-off.
